questions.title: Define a prototype
questions.text: Define the term **prototype** in system development.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- An early / simplified working model of the system or part of it (1)
- showing how it will look and work so users can test it and give feedback (1)
scheme.model_answer: An early, simplified model of the new system that shows its screens and behaviour so that users can try it and give feedback.

questions.title: Advantage of prototyping
questions.text: Give **one** advantage of using a prototype in a project.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any one (1): easy detection of missing functionality; quick feedback; reduced time and costs; developers and users understand the system better; users involved / accept the system

questions.title: Disadvantage of prototyping
questions.text: Give **one** disadvantage of using a prototype in a project.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any one (1): additional development costs; time-consuming; constrains the designer's ideas; may hide the complexity; users expect the final system too soon; scope creep

questions.title: Advantage or disadvantage
questions.text: Tick (✓) to show whether each statement is an advantage or a disadvantage of prototyping.

prefill: Users give quick feedback on the screens
Users may think the prototype is the finished system
The prototype design can constrain the designer's ideas

scheme.mark_scheme: 1 Advantage (1); 2 Disadvantage (1); 3 Advantage (1); 4 Disadvantage (1)

questions.title: Types of prototype
questions.text: Match each type of prototype to its description.

right.text: Built quickly to clarify requirements, then discarded
Improved step by step until it becomes the final system

scheme.mark_scheme: L1–R1, L2–R2, L3–R3. One mark per correct match.

questions.title: Prototyping cycle
questions.text:
Complete the sentences.

The developer builds the prototype, users [[1]] it and give [[2]], and the developer [[3]] the prototype. This is repeated until the users are satisfied.

scheme.mark_scheme: (1) test / try / evaluate (2) feedback (3) refines / improves / changes / modifies

questions.title: Prototypes and cost
questions.text: Building a prototype costs money, yet it can **reduce** the total cost of a project. Explain why.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Errors / missing requirements are found early, before coding the full system (1)
- changes are cheaper early than after the system is built / fewer changes after delivery (1)
scheme.model_answer: Users find missing or wrong requirements while testing the prototype, and fixing them at this stage is much cheaper than changing the finished system later.

questions.title: Choose controls
questions.text: Tick (✓) the most suitable input control for each field of a club registration form.

scheme.mark_scheme: Name → text box (1); Grade → drop-down (1); Membership → radio buttons (1); Agree → check box (1)

questions.title: Why a drop-down
questions.text: Explain why a drop-down list is used for the field "City" on an input form.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- The user selects from a fixed list (1)
- so spelling errors / invalid cities are prevented / faster entry / saves space (1)
scheme.model_answer: The user picks the city from a list, so it cannot be misspelt and only valid cities are entered.

questions.title: Good input forms
questions.text: State **two** features of a well-designed input form.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): fields in logical order; clear labels; suitable controls; validation with error messages; required fields marked; hints / placeholders; Save / Clear buttons; consistent layout
scheme.model_answer: 1 Clear labels next to each field. 2 Error messages when data is invalid.

questions.title: Good output forms
questions.text: State **two** features of a well-designed output form (report).

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): title and date; data in tables with headings; totals / summaries; only needed information; charts; page numbers; print / export option
scheme.model_answer: 1 A clear title and date. 2 Data in a table with column headings and totals.

questions.title: Build a form prototype
questions.text: Write HTML for a prototype of a library **book-search** form with: a text box for the title, a drop-down list of genres (Fiction, History, Science), a check box "Available only" and a **Search** button.

scheme.mark_scheme: Labelled text box for title (1); select with the three genres (1); checkbox Available only (1); Search button inside a form (1)
scheme.model_answer:
<form>
  <label>Title <input type="text" name="title"></label>
  <label>Genre
    <select name="genre">
      <option>Fiction</option><option>History</option><option>Science</option>
    </select>
  </label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="available"> Available only</label>
  <button type="submit">Search</button>
</form>

questions.title: Administrator prototype
questions.text: It is planned that an online store will have an administrator mode. The administrator will be responsible for viewing and managing the orders. Describe (or sketch in text) a prototype of the administrator screen. Label each component.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Order table with attributes (1)
Main menu / navigation (1)
At least two buttons with names (save / edit / delete / navigation) (2)
[max 4] Other correct controls accepted.
scheme.model_answer: Top: a navigation bar with Orders, Products, Customers and Log out. Centre: a table of orders with columns Order no., Customer, Date, Total and Status. Bottom: buttons Edit, Delete and Save, and a drop-down to change the order status.

questions.title: Prototype for a clinic
questions.text: A software company is developing an appointment app for a clinic. The receptionists are not sure exactly which features they need. Discuss whether the company should build a prototype first.

scheme.mark_scheme: Up to 4: requirements unclear — prototype lets receptionists try screens and clarify needs (1); missing functions found early / quick feedback (1); cheaper changes before full coding (1); drawbacks — extra time / cost, receptionists may expect the finished app, scope creep (1); justified conclusion (1)
scheme.model_answer: Because the receptionists do not know exactly what they need, a prototype would let them try the booking screens and say what is missing, so problems are found before the full app is coded, when changes are cheap. It would take extra time and money, and the receptionists might expect the finished app immediately, but the company should still build a prototype because unclear requirements are the biggest risk.

questions.title: Prototyping
questions.text: A developer uses prototyping to develop an online store.

scheme.mark_scheme: Early / simplified model of the system (1); used to show the design and get user feedback (1)
scheme.model_answer: An early working model of the system that shows how it will look and work so users can give feedback.

parts.title: Advantage and disadvantage
parts.text: Give **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage of using a prototype in a project.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Advantage (1): easy detection of missing functionality; quick feedback; reduced time and costs; better understanding
Disadvantage (1): prototype design can constrain a designer's ideas; complexity may be hidden; extra cost; time consuming
scheme.model_answer: Advantage: quick feedback from users. Disadvantage: additional development costs.

scheme.mark_scheme: Throw-away: built to clarify requirements then discarded (1); evolutionary: refined until it becomes the final system (1)
scheme.model_answer: A throw-away prototype is discarded after it has clarified the requirements, whereas an evolutionary prototype is improved until it becomes the final system.

parts.title: User involvement
parts.text: Explain how involving users in testing the prototype benefits the final system.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Users' feedback shows missing / wrong features (1)
- so the final system meets their needs / they accept it more easily (1)
scheme.model_answer: Users point out missing or confusing features, so the final store meets their needs and they are happier to use it.

questions.title: An input form
questions.text: Customers of the online store register with: full name, e-mail, city (one of 17 regional centres), delivery type (courier or pick-up point), and agreement to the terms.

parts.title: Controls
parts.text: Tick (✓) the most suitable control for each field.

scheme.mark_scheme: E-mail text box (1); City drop-down (1); Delivery radio buttons (1); Agreement check box (1)

parts.title: Prototype
parts.text: Write HTML for a prototype of the registration form with labels for: full name, city (show at least two options), delivery type, agreement to the terms, and a **Register** button.

scheme.mark_scheme: Text box for name with label (1); select with at least two cities (1); two radio buttons with the same name for delivery (1); checkbox for agreement and Register button (1)
scheme.model_answer:
<form>
  <label>Full name <input type="text" name="name"></label>
  <label>City <select name="city"><option>Astana</option><option>Almaty</option></select></label>
  <input type="radio" name="delivery" value="courier"> Courier
  <input type="radio" name="delivery" value="pickup"> Pick-up point
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="agree"> I agree to the terms</label>
  <button type="submit">Register</button>
</form>

questions.title: Administrator mode
questions.text: It is planned that the online store will have an administrator mode. The administrator will be responsible for viewing and managing the orders.

parts.title: Admin screen
parts.text: Draw (describe in text) the prototype of the administrator interface. Label each component.

scheme.mark_scheme: order table with attributes (1); main menu / navigation (1); at least two buttons with name (save / edit / delete / navigation) (2) [max 4] Other correct controls accepted.
scheme.model_answer: Navigation bar: Orders | Products | Customers | Log out. Table of orders with Order no., Customer, Date, Total, Status. Buttons: Edit, Delete, Save.

parts.title: Report
parts.text: The administrator also needs a daily sales report. State **two** features of a well-designed output form for this report.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): title and date; table with headings; totals; only needed information; chart; print / export
scheme.model_answer: 1 A title with the date of the report. 2 A total of the day's sales at the bottom.

parts.title: Feedback
parts.text: Explain how the developer should use the administrator's feedback on the prototype.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Change / refine the prototype to add missing features or fix problems (1)
- test again with the administrator until satisfied, then build the final system (1)
scheme.model_answer: The developer changes the prototype to fix the problems the administrator found, then asks her to test it again, repeating until she is satisfied before building the final version.

summary: What a prototype is, throw-away and evolutionary prototyping, the advantages and disadvantages of using prototypes, and how to design prototypes of the interface, input forms and output forms of a new system.

blocks.content: An **early, simplified working model** of a new system (or part of it) that shows **how it will look and behave** — its screens, menus, forms and reports — so that users can **try it and give feedback** before the full system is built.

A prototype usually has the **interface** but only part of the **functionality**: buttons may not save data yet, and calculations may use example values. The developer changes the prototype after each round of user feedback.

flowchart TB
  A[Identify basic requirements] --> B[Build the prototype]
  B --> C[Users test the prototype]
  C --> D[Collect feedback]
  D --> E{Users satisfied?}
  E -- No --> F[Refine the prototype]
  F --> C
  E -- Yes --> G[Build / complete the final system]
blocks.caption: The prototyping cycle

blocks.title: Types of prototype
rows: Built quickly to **clarify requirements**; then **discarded** and the real system is built from scratch
Paper sketches or a clickable mock-up of an app's screens
Improved step by step until it **becomes the final system**
A web shop that starts with a catalogue page and grows with each version
Paper sketches, wireframes — quick and cheap
Looks and behaves almost like the real system
An interactive mock-up made in Figma or HTML

items.title: Advantages
items.content:
- **Users see and try** the system early, so **missing or wrong requirements** are found quickly (easy detection of missing functionality).
- **Quick feedback** from users improves the design.
- Users and developers **understand the system better**; fewer misunderstandings.
- Errors are found **early**, when they are **cheaper** to fix → **reduced time and costs** overall.
- Users feel **involved**, so they **accept** the final system more easily.
- The prototype can be used for **training** and for the **user guide**.

items.title: Disadvantages
items.content:
- Building prototypes adds **additional development cost** and is **time-consuming**.
- Users may think the prototype **is the finished system** and expect it too soon.
- Users may keep asking for **changes** (scope creep), so the project grows.
- The prototype design can **constrain the designer's ideas** — later better solutions are ignored.
- If the designer's knowledge is limited, the prototype may **hide the real complexity** of the system.
- Quick prototype code may be **poorly structured** if it is kept (evolutionary).

blocks.content: Give a **specific** effect: not "it is good", but "*users can test the input form early, so missing fields are added before the system is coded*".

items.title: Interface (navigation) design
items.content:
- A **main menu** or navigation bar that leads to every part of the system.
- **Consistent** layout, colours, fonts and button positions on every screen.
- Clear **headings** so the user knows where they are; a **Back / Home** button.
- **Help** messages and tooltips.
- Suitable for the **users** (large buttons for a touchscreen kiosk, simple words for children).

items.title: Input form design
items.content:
- Fields in a **logical order** (as on the paper form).
- Clear **labels** next to each field; examples / hints in placeholders.
- Suitable **controls**: text box, drop-down list, radio buttons, check box, date picker.
- **Validation** and clear **error messages**; required fields marked *.
- **Buttons**: Save, Clear, Cancel.

items.title: Output form (report) design
items.content:
- A clear **title**, date and page numbers.
- Data in **tables** with column headings; **totals** and summaries.
- Only the information the user **needs**; charts where helpful.
- Can be **printed** or **exported** (PDF).

blocks.title: Choosing input controls
rows: Choice from a long fixed list (category, city)
One of a few options (gender, payment type)
All options visible; exactly one chosen
Yes / No (best-sale product, agree to terms)

blocks.title: How to develop a prototype for a scenario
items: List the **requirements**: which screens, which data must be entered, which reports are needed.
For each **input form**, list the fields, choose a **control** for each and add **validation**.
For each **output form**, choose the layout (table, totals, chart).
Build the prototype (paper, slides, Figma, HTML, a form designer in the programming tool).
**Test** it with users, collect **feedback**, and **refine** it.

blocks.title: Exam-style answers
blocks.content:
**Q: Give one advantage of using a prototype in a project. [1]**
**Easy detection of missing functionality** / quick feedback / reduced time and costs / helps developers and users understand the system better.

**Q: Write one disadvantage of using a prototype when developing a new system. [1]**
**Additional development costs** / it is **time-consuming** / prototype design can constrain a designer's ideas.

**Q: Explain why a drop-down list is used for "Category" on the input form. [2]**
The user **chooses from a fixed list** (1), so **spelling errors and invalid categories** are prevented / it saves space (1).

- Saying the prototype **is** the final system (unless it is evolutionary).
- Drawing a form without **labels** or without the **fields** listed in the question.
- Choosing a text box where a list or radio buttons would prevent errors.
- Forgetting **buttons** and **navigation** in an interface prototype.
